title.en: Self-supervised learning: labels from the data itself
title.zh: 自监督学习：从数据本身造标签

description.en: Why unlabelled data is enough to learn from, pretext tasks, the contrastive (InfoNCE) loss term by term with numbers, why the representations transfer, and how next-token prediction becomes a language model.
description.zh: 为什么没有标注也能学，前置任务有哪些，对比损失（InfoNCE）逐项拆开并带数字算一遍，表示为什么能迁移，以及“预测下一个词”怎么变成语言模型。

name.zh: 前置任务与预训练—迁移流程
下一词预测与语言模型
大模型训练：预训练再微调

description.en: Treating self-supervised learning as just unsupervised learning (it has a target and a loss; the goal is a reusable representation)
description.zh: 把自监督当成普通的无监督学习（它有目标和损失，目的是得到可复用的表示）

description.en: Believing no labels are ever needed (the downstream task still needs a few)
description.zh: 以为从头到尾都不需要标注（下游任务仍要少量标注）

description.en: Thinking a smaller temperature is always better (it concentrates the push on hard negatives, including false ones)
description.zh: 以为温度越小越好（它把力集中在难负样本上，包括被误判的负样本）

description.en: Thinking a language model needs human-written labels for next-token prediction
description.zh: 以为下一词预测需要人工写的标签

title.en: Why: labels are expensive, raw data is not
title.zh: 为什么：标注贵，原始数据便宜

text.en: Supervised learning is limited by labels. A label costs a person's time (a doctor reading a scan, a student marking sentences); raw images and raw text are nearly free. **Self-supervised learning (SSL)** takes the one thing that is abundant and *manufactures* the labels from it: **supervision does not have to come from humans.**
text.zh: 监督学习被标注卡住：一条标签要花人的时间（医生看片子、学生标句子），而原始图片和文本几乎是免费的。**自监督学习 (self-supervised learning, SSL)** 就是用最充裕的东西——数据本身——去*造*标签：**监督信号不一定要来自人。**

rows.en: data with a part removed or corrupted
rows.zh: 被遮掉/破坏一部分的数据
被遮掉的/原来的那部分

text.en: Example from the lecture: hide a patch of a cat photo and ask the model to predict it. The label (the patch) came from the image itself, with no annotation. To get it right the model must learn texture, shape and what a cat's eye looks like. *We never told it 'cat'; it works it out because it has to.*
text.zh: 讲义里的例子：把猫图里的一小块遮掉，让模型把它预测出来。标签（那一小块）来自图片本身，没有任何人工标注。要预测对，模型必须学会纹理、形状、猫眼长什么样。*没人告诉它“这是猫”，是任务逼着它自己弄明白的。*

rows.zh: 由 x 自己造的目标

text.en: Two contrasts the exam likes. **Versus unsupervised:** SSL *has* a target and a loss, trained by gradient descent exactly like supervised learning; what is unsupervised is only where the target comes from. And its product is a representation for later use, not the answer to the pretext task. **Versus semi-supervised:** semi-supervised learning mixes labelled and unlabelled data in *one* training (self-training, graph methods); SSL learns on unlabelled data in a *first stage*, then a second stage uses labels.
text.zh: 考试常问两组对比。**对无监督：** SSL *有*目标、有损失，用梯度下降训练，和监督学习一样；“无监督”的只是目标从哪来。而且它的产出是一个留给后面用的表示，不是前置任务本身的答案。**对半监督：** 半监督把有/无标注数据放在*同一次*训练里（自训练、图方法）；SSL 先在无标注数据上学*第一阶段*，第二阶段才用标签。

prompt.en: A model is trained to colour in grey-scale photos, using the original colour photos as targets. Which setting is this?
prompt.zh: 用原来的彩色照片当目标，训练模型给灰度照片上色。这属于哪种设定？

label.en: Unsupervised: there are no labels
label.zh: 无监督：没有标签

feedback.en: There is a target (the original colours) and a loss. Unsupervised methods have no target at all.
feedback.zh: 它有目标（原色）和损失；无监督方法根本没有目标。

label.en: Self-supervised: the target is made from the data
label.zh: 自监督：目标由数据本身造出

label.en: Semi-supervised: a few labels guide it
label.zh: 半监督：有少量标签指导

feedback.en: No human label is used here; semi-supervised learning needs some labelled instances.
feedback.zh: 这里没用任何人工标签；半监督需要一部分有标注的样本。

explain.en: The colour photo gives both the input (grey version) and the target (the colours). No human labelled anything, yet there is a loss to minimise.
explain.zh: 彩色照片既给出输入（灰度版）又给出目标（颜色）。没有人工标注，却有损失可以最小化。

alt.en: Stage 1 trains an encoder on unlabelled data with a pretext task; stage 2 freezes it and trains a small head on a few labels.
alt.zh: 第一阶段用前置任务在无标注数据上训练编码器；第二阶段冻结它，只用少量标注训练小分类头。

text.en: **Pretext task:** the made-up task whose labels come free from the data. Its only purpose is to force the **encoder** (an FNN, a Transformer, ...) to produce a useful **representation**. **Downstream task:** the task we actually care about, with few human labels. The encoder is **frozen** (kept as learned) and only a small fully-connected layer on top is trained. That is far cheaper than training from scratch on many labels: we 'warm-start' from the pretext task.
text.zh: **前置任务 (pretext task)：** 标签免费来自数据的“自造任务”。它唯一的作用是逼**编码器**（FNN、Transformer 等）学出有用的**表示 (representation)**。**下游任务 (downstream task)：** 我们真正关心的任务，只有少量人工标签。编码器被**冻结**（保持学到的样子），只训练它上面一个小的全连接层。这比用大量标签从头训练便宜得多：我们从前置任务“热启动”。

rows.zh: 遮住输入的一部分，把它还原

summary.en: More pretext tasks you may meet (textbook, not in the deck)
summary.zh: 其他常见前置任务（教科书内容，讲义没有）

items.en: **Rotation prediction:** rotate the image by 0/90/180/270 degrees, classify which; to answer, the model must recognise what is up in a scene.
items.zh: **旋转预测：** 把图旋转 0/90/180/270 度，分类是哪一种；要答对就得认出场景里什么是“上”。

items.en: **Jigsaw:** cut the image into tiles, shuffle, predict the permutation; requires knowing how parts of an object fit.
items.zh: **拼图：** 把图切成块并打乱，预测排列；需要知道物体各部分怎么拼。

items.en: **Colourisation, inpainting:** predict the colours or the removed region from the rest.
items.zh: **上色、补全：** 由其余部分预测颜色或被抠掉的区域。

items.en: **Masked language modelling:** mask about 15% of the words, predict them from both sides (BERT).
items.zh: **掩码语言模型：** 遮住约 15% 的词，用左右两侧上下文预测（BERT）。

text.en: All three share the recipe: **change or hide something in the data; the unchanged data is the answer.**
text.zh: 三种办法套路相同：**对数据做点改动或遮挡，没改动的原数据就是答案。**

alt.en: A SimCLR-style pipeline: two augmented views of one image go through the same encoder f and a projection g; their outputs z_i, z_j are pulled together and pushed away from the outputs of other images.
alt.zh: SimCLR 式流程：同一张图的两个增强视图经过同一个编码器 f 和投影 g；输出 z_i、z_j 被拉近，并与其他图像的输出推远。

text.en: There is no 'next word' or 'missing patch' to predict here. The label is a **relationship**. Take an image and make two random **augmentations** of it (crop, flip, colour change, blur): these two views form a **positive pair**. Views of *other* images in the batch are **negatives**. Train so that positives get similar embeddings and negatives get dissimilar ones.
text.zh: 这里没有“下一个词”或“缺失的块”要预测，标签是一种**关系**。取一张图，做两种随机**增强**（裁剪、翻转、变色、模糊）：这两个视图是一个**正样本对 (positive pair)**；同一批里*别的*图像的视图是**负样本 (negatives)**。训练目标：正样本嵌入相似，负样本嵌入不相似。

items.en: **Augmentations carry the bias:** they say what should be ignored (position, colour) and so what is kept (the object).
items.zh: **增强决定偏置：** 它规定了应该忽略什么（位置、颜色），也就决定了留下什么（物体本身）。

items.en: **Projection head g** (SimCLR, textbook): the loss is computed on z = g(f(x)); after pre-training g is thrown away and the encoder output is used downstream.
items.zh: **投影头 g**（SimCLR，教科书内容）：损失在 z = g(f(x)) 上算；预训练完扔掉 g，下游使用编码器输出。

items.en: **Negatives come free** from the same batch: with N images there are 2N views, and each view has 2(N−1) negatives.
items.zh: **负样本从同一批里免费得到：** N 张图有 2N 个视图，每个视图有 2(N−1) 个负样本。

title.en: Deeper: the contrastive loss (InfoNCE) term by term
title.zh: 深入：对比损失（InfoNCE）逐项推导

say.en: Compare the anchor $a$ with each candidate $k$ by **cosine similarity**: 1 if they point the same way, 0 if unrelated, −1 if opposite. Candidate 0 is the positive, candidates 1..K are negatives.
say.zh: 用**余弦相似度**比较锚点 $a$ 和每个候选 $k$：方向相同为 1，无关为 0，相反为 −1。候选 0 是正样本，1..K 是负样本。

why.en: Normalising means only direction counts; the loss cannot be lowered just by making vectors longer.
why.zh: 归一化之后只有方向有意义；不能靠把向量拉长来降低损失。

say.en: Divide by the **temperature** $\tau > 0$. It will control how sharply the loss separates a small lead from a large one.
say.zh: 除以**温度** $\tau > 0$。它控制损失对“小领先”和“大领先”区分得多尖锐。

say.en: Softmax over the $K+1$ candidates. $p_0$ is the model's probability that the positive is the true partner of the anchor: we have turned the problem into a **classification** with one correct class.
say.zh: 对 $K+1$ 个候选做 softmax。$p_0$ 是模型认为“正样本才是锚点真伙伴”的概率：问题变成了只有一个正确类的**分类**。

say.en: The usual cross-entropy with the positive as the right class. This is **InfoNCE**; SimCLR calls it NT-Xent (normalised temperature-scaled cross-entropy).
say.zh: 就是以正样本为正确类的交叉熵。这就是 **InfoNCE**；SimCLR 叫它 NT-Xent（归一化、带温度的交叉熵）。

say.en: Split the log. **(1), the numerator:** rewards a high similarity to the positive (pull). **(2), the denominator:** a smooth maximum of *all* similarities; any candidate that looks like the anchor raises it (push). The positive is inside the denominator too, so the loss cannot be driven down by inflating everything.
say.zh: 把对数拆开。**(1) 分子：** 奖励与正样本的高相似度（拉）。**(2) 分母：** 对*所有*相似度取平滑最大值；任何长得像锚点的候选都会把它抬高（推）。正样本自己也在分母里，所以不能靠把所有相似度一起抬高来降低损失。

say.en: Gradient on the positive's similarity: negative, so gradient descent *raises* $s_0$. The pull fades as $p_0 \to 1$.
say.zh: 对正样本相似度的梯度：为负，所以梯度下降会*抬高* $s_0$。当 $p_0 \to 1$ 时拉力渐弱。

say.en: Each negative is pushed down with strength $p_k$: the ones that currently look most like the anchor (**hard negatives**) are pushed hardest, easy ones hardly at all.
say.zh: 每个负样本以强度 $p_k$ 被往下推：现在最像锚点的那些（**难负样本**）推得最狠，容易的几乎不推。

say.en: Sanity check: if the model cannot tell the candidates apart, every $p_j = 1/(K+1)$, which is the 'know nothing' level $\ln(K+1)$.
say.zh: 自检：如果模型完全分不出候选，则每个 $p_j = 1/(K+1)$，损失就是“什么都不知道”的水平 $\ln(K+1)$。

intro.en: Instead of inventing separate attract and repel terms, treat the job as a multiple-choice question: *among 1 positive and K negatives, which one is the true partner of this anchor?*
intro.zh: 不去分别发明“吸引项”和“排斥项”，而是把任务当成一道选择题：*在 1 个正样本和 K 个负样本里，哪一个才是这个锚点的真伙伴？*

outro.en: In a batch the loss is averaged over all anchors. Pull and push come from one formula: numerator pulls, denominator pushes.
outro.zh: 在一个批里，对所有锚点取平均。拉和推出自同一个式子：分子拉，分母推。

title.en: Deeper: InfoNCE for one anchor, by hand
title.zh: 深入：手算一个锚点的 InfoNCE

say.en: One anchor, one positive (0.8) and three negatives. The first negative (0.5) is a hard one: nearly as similar as the positive. Take $\tau = 0.5$.
say.zh: 一个锚点，一个正样本（0.8）和三个负样本。第一个负样本（0.5）是难的：几乎和正样本一样相似。取 $\tau = 0.5$。

say.en: Divide every similarity by $\tau$.
say.zh: 每个相似度除以 $\tau$。

say.en: Exponentiate (calculator).
say.zh: 取指数（用计算器）。

say.en: The denominator: add the four.
say.zh: 分母：四项相加。

say.en: The positive's softmax probability: numerator over denominator.
say.zh: 正样本的 softmax 概率：分子除以分母。

say.en: Take $-\ln$. For comparison the 'know nothing' level is $\ln 4 = 1.386$.
say.zh: 取 $-\ln$。对照：“什么都不知道”的水平是 $\ln 4 = 1.386$。

say.en: The gradients: the positive is pulled up with $(1-p_0)/\tau$; each negative is pushed down with $p_k/\tau$. The hard negative takes half of the push. They sum to zero: total pull equals total push.
say.zh: 梯度：正样本以 $(1-p_0)/\tau$ 被拉高；每个负样本以 $p_k/\tau$ 被压低。难负样本承担了一半的推力。它们加起来为零：总拉力等于总推力。

intro.en: The recipe is the same as the exam would ask: similarities in, loss out. Natural log throughout.
intro.zh: 套路和考试会问的一样：给相似度，求损失。全程自然对数。

prompt.en: Write $p_0$ as a fraction of the four exponentials from $u$.
prompt.zh: 把 $p_0$ 写成关于 $u$ 的四个指数项的分式。

alt.en: The same four similarities turned into softmax probabilities at three temperatures: the lower the temperature, the more the positive and the hardest negative take everything.
alt.zh: 同样四个相似度在三个温度下变成的 softmax 概率：温度越低，概率越集中到正样本和最难的负样本上。

head.en: share of the push on the hardest negative
head.zh: 推力中落在最难负样本上的比例

text.en: **Lower τ** sharpens the softmax: differences are magnified, the loss and its gradient care almost only about the *hardest* negatives, which helps the model learn fine distinctions. **Higher τ** flattens it: all negatives are treated alike, and as $\tau \to \infty$ the loss tends to $\ln(K+1)$ with a weak signal.
text.zh: **τ 变小**让 softmax 更尖：差异被放大，损失和梯度几乎只关心*最难*的负样本，有利于学到细微区别。**τ 变大**让它变平：所有负样本一视同仁，$\tau \to \infty$ 时损失趋于 $\ln(K+1)$，信号很弱。

title.en: Smaller is not simply better
title.zh: τ 并不是越小越好

body.en: Suppose the 'hardest negative' is a *false negative*: another photo of the same dog that happens to be in the batch. With similarities (0.5, 0.9, 0.1, −0.3) the loss is 1.28 at τ = 1 but 4.02 at τ = 0.1, and nearly all the push goes to that very photo. A low temperature punishes label noise hardest.
body.zh: 假设“最难的负样本”其实是*假负样本*：批里恰好有同一条狗的另一张照片。相似度 (0.5, 0.9, 0.1, −0.3) 时，τ = 1 的损失是 1.28，τ = 0.1 却是 4.02，而且几乎所有推力都砸在那张照片上。温度低，对标签噪声的惩罚最重。

prompt.en: You lower τ from 0.5 to 0.1 on the same similarities. What changes?
prompt.zh: 同样的相似度，τ 从 0.5 降到 0.1，会怎样？

label.en: The push is spread more evenly over all negatives
label.zh: 推力在所有负样本之间分得更均匀

feedback.en: That is what a *higher* τ does. Lower τ concentrates it.
feedback.zh: 那是*更高*的 τ 的效果；τ 低会更集中。

label.en: The push concentrates on the hardest negative
label.zh: 推力更集中在最难的负样本上

label.en: The loss can no longer go below ln(K+1)
label.zh: 损失再也低不过 ln(K+1)

feedback.en: ln(K+1) is the loss at *no* discrimination, and lower τ lets the loss go lower, not stay higher.
feedback.zh: ln(K+1) 是毫无区分度时的损失；τ 越低，损失反而可以更低。

explain.en: Softmax with a small temperature is nearly an argmax: only the biggest similarities matter, so the gradient lands on the hardest negative.
explain.zh: 小温度的 softmax 接近 argmax：只有最大的相似度才起作用，梯度就落在最难的负样本上。

title.en: Deeper: why these representations transfer
title.zh: 深入：为什么这样学到的表示能迁移

text.en: Nobody asked the encoder to recognise dogs, yet a linear layer on top of it can. The reason is in what the pretext task *forces*:
text.zh: 没人要求编码器认识狗，但在它上面加一层线性层就能认。原因在于前置任务*逼着*它做什么：

items.en: **Contrastive:** to put two crops/colour-shifted views of one photo close together, the encoder must keep what survives those changes (shape, parts, texture of the object) and drop what does not (position, exact colour). To keep different photos apart it must keep what distinguishes them. What survives *and* distinguishes is mostly semantic.
items.zh: **对比：** 要让同一张照片的两个裁剪/变色视图靠近，编码器就必须保留经得住这些变化的东西（物体的形状、部件、纹理），丢掉经不住的（位置、确切颜色）；要把不同照片分开，就必须保留能区分它们的东西。既经得住变化*又*能区分的，多半是语义。

items.en: **Masked / autoregressive:** to fill in a patch you must know what objects look like; to predict a next word you need grammar, facts and common sense. The deepest regularities of the data are what lower the loss.
items.zh: **遮挡/自回归：** 要补出一块图，得知道物体长什么样；要预测下一个词，得懂语法、事实和常识。数据里最深的规律才能降低损失。

items.en: **Pretext and downstream need the same information.** The downstream labels (cat, dog) depend on exactly the structure that the encoder had to learn, so a small head suffices.
items.zh: **前置任务和下游任务需要同样的信息。** 下游标签（猫、狗）依赖的正是编码器被迫学会的结构，所以小小的头就够了。

text.en: The deeper reason (van den Oord et al., 2018; textbook): minimising InfoNCE *maximises a lower bound on the mutual information between the two views*. The shared information of two views of the same thing is its content. The bound cannot exceed $\ln(K+1)$, so more negatives (a bigger batch) let the model capture more.
text.zh: 更深的原因（van den Oord 等，2018；教科书内容）：最小化 InfoNCE 就是在*最大化两个视图之间互信息的下界*。同一事物的两个视图共有的信息就是它的内容。这个下界不会超过 $\ln(K+1)$，所以负样本越多（批越大），模型能抓到的越多。

title.en: When transfer fails
title.zh: 什么时候迁移会失败

body.en: (1) The pretext can be solved with a **shortcut** that has nothing to do with meaning (for jigsaw, the colour fringes at tile edges give the answer away). (2) The augmentation **throws away what the downstream task needs** (colour jitter ruins a task that classifies ripeness by colour). (3) The pre-training data differs from the target data. SSL representations also inherit the **biases of the data** they were trained on (see the fairness lesson).
body.zh: (1) 前置任务能用与语义无关的**捷径**解出来（拼图里，块边缘的色边就泄露了答案）。(2) 增强**丢掉了下游任务需要的信息**（用颜色判断成熟度的任务，颜色抖动就毁了它）。(3) 预训练数据和目标数据差太远。SSL 学到的表示还会继承训练数据里的**偏差**（见公平性那一课）。

title.en: Why next-token prediction is self-supervised
title.zh: 为什么“预测下一个词”是自监督

say.en: A text of $T$ tokens (words or word pieces). No label anywhere.
say.zh: 一段含 $T$ 个词元 (token) 的文本。哪里都没有标签。

say.en: At every position $t$, the words before it are the input and the word that really comes next is the target. One text gives $T$ labelled examples for free. **That is why it is self-supervised: the label comes from the data itself.**
say.zh: 在每个位置 $t$，它前面的词是输入，真正出现的下一个词是目标。一段文本免费给出 $T$ 个带标签的样本。**这就是它属于自监督的原因：标签来自数据本身。**

say.en: The chain rule of probability: exact, no assumption. A bigram model would keep only $x_{t-1}$; an LLM conditions on the whole left context.
say.zh: 概率的链式法则：精确成立，不需要任何假设。二元模型只保留 $x_{t-1}$；大模型以整个左侧上下文为条件。

say.en: Cross-entropy between the model's next-token distribution and the one-hot true token, summed over positions. It equals the **negative log-likelihood of the text**, so training is maximum likelihood estimation, as in the probability lesson.
say.zh: 模型的下一词分布与独热真实词之间的交叉熵，对各位置求和。它就是**文本的负对数似然**，所以训练就是极大似然估计，和概率那一课一样。

say.en: Example on 'the cat sat on the mat'. Probabilities the model gave to the true next word: cat|the = 0.05, sat|the cat = 0.2, on|...sat = 0.5, the|...on = 0.4, mat|...the = 0.1. Add the five $-\ln p$.
say.zh: 例子：“the cat sat on the mat”。模型给真实下一个词的概率：cat|the = 0.05，sat|the cat = 0.2，on|…sat = 0.5，the|…on = 0.4，mat|…the = 0.1。把五个 $-\ln p$ 加起来。

say.en: Per-token loss, and its exponential, the **perplexity**: the model is as unsure as if it chose uniformly among about 5.5 words at each step. Lower is better.
say.zh: 每个词元的平均损失，及其指数——**困惑度 (perplexity)**：模型的不确定程度，相当于每一步在约 5.5 个词里均匀乱猜。越低越好。

intro.en: A sentence already contains its own labels. Take 'the cat sat on the mat'.
intro.zh: 一个句子里已经带着它自己的标签。以“the cat sat on the mat”为例。

outro.en: Because the Transformer decoder only looks left (it cannot peek at the answer), all $T$ predictions of a text are computed in a single pass. GPT-3 needed no other supervision than this.
outro.zh: Transformer 解码器只看左边（不能偷看答案），所以一段文本的 $T$ 个预测一次前向就能全算出来。GPT-3 除此之外没用别的监督。

prompt.en: Write the total loss as a sum of the five $-\ln p$ terms.
prompt.zh: 把总损失写成五项 $-\ln p$ 之和。

title.en: From counting to a neural language model
title.zh: 从数数到神经语言模型

text.en: A **language model** gives the probability of the next word. The oldest way is counting.
text.zh: **语言模型**给出下一个词的概率。最古老的办法是数数。

rows.zh: P(w | 前一词) = count(前一词, w) / count(前一词)

rows.en: a neural network trained by next-token loss
rows.zh: 用下一词损失训练的神经网络

rows.en: needs lots of data and compute

text.en: **Why n-grams fail:** with a vocabulary of V = 50,000 words, a 5-gram has V⁴ = 6.25×10^18 different 4-word contexts, while even 10¹³ training tokens could cover only a tiny fraction of them. Most contexts were never seen, so counting gives no estimate. Sentences like *'The water wasn't just hot, it was ___'* or *'The square root of 9 is ___'* need a model that **generalises** from what it has seen, not one that only counts.
text.zh: **n 元为什么不行：** 词表 V = 50,000 时，5 元组有 V⁴ = 6.25×10^18 种 4 词上下文，而哪怕 10¹³ 个训练词元也只能覆盖其中极小一部分。绝大多数上下文从没见过，数数就给不出估计。像 *“The water wasn't just hot, it was ___”*、*“The square root of 9 is ___”* 这样的句子，需要的是能从见过的东西中**泛化**的模型，而不是只会数数的。

prompt.en: Why does a 5-gram model fail on long, rare contexts while a neural LM does not?
prompt.zh: 为什么 5 元模型在长而罕见的上下文上失灵，神经语言模型却不会？

label.en: Counts for unseen contexts are zero or undefined; a neural net shares what it learned between similar contexts
label.zh: 没见过的上下文计数为零或无定义；神经网络把学到的东西在相似上下文间共享

label.en: A neural net memorises every sentence it saw
label.zh: 神经网络把见过的每句话都背下来

feedback.en: Memorising would fail on new contexts just as counting does; the gain is generalisation.
feedback.zh: 死记同样会在新上下文上失败；神经网络的好处是泛化。

label.en: N-grams cannot use unlabelled text
label.zh: n 元模型不能用无标注文本

feedback.en: They use only raw text; the problem is sparsity, not labels.
feedback.zh: 它们用的就是原始文本；问题在稀疏，而不在标签。

explain.en: Estimating by counting needs each context to have been seen. A neural LM represents words as vectors, so similar contexts get similar predictions.
explain.zh: 靠数数估计，要求每个上下文都见过。神经语言模型把词表示成向量，相似的上下文得到相似的预测。

title.en: What model do we actually need?
title.zh: 我们究竟需要什么样的模型？

text.en: Three needs from the lecture: capture the **relationship between words** (meaning, order); handle **long-range dependencies** (what was said ten words ago can matter now); and **generalise** to combinations never seen. A plain FNN fails the first two:
text.zh: 讲义里的三个需求：抓住**词与词的关系**（含义、顺序）；处理**长程依赖**（十个词前说的话现在可能还重要）；对没见过的组合**泛化**。普通 FNN 前两条都做不到：

items.en: **No order.** An FNN on a bag of words treats 'The dog is chasing the cat' and 'The cat is chasing the dog' as the same input; it does not care which word is $x_1$ and which is $x_3$.
items.zh: **没有顺序。** 词袋输入的 FNN 把“The dog is chasing the cat”和“The cat is chasing the dog”当成同一个输入；它不在乎哪个词是 $x_1$、哪个是 $x_3$。

items.en: **No links within a layer.** Nodes only connect across layers, so there is no way to relate 'it' to 'trophy' in 'The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big' (and to 'suitcase' if the last word is 'small'). That needs common sense about relations.
items.zh: **同层节点没有连接。** 节点只在层与层之间相连，所以没法把“The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big”里的 it 和 trophy 联系起来（结尾换成 small，it 就指 suitcase）。这需要关于关系的常识。

title.en: Positional encoding: telling the model where each word is
title.zh: 位置编码：告诉模型每个词在哪

text.en: Each token first becomes a dense vector (its **embedding**; the same word always gives the same vector). Then a **positional vector** of alternating sines and cosines is *added*, so the model receives a vector that mixes *what* the word is with *where* it is. 'the' at position 0 and 'the' at position 3 now have different vectors.
text.zh: 每个词元先变成一个稠密向量（**词嵌入**；同一个词总得到同一个向量）。然后*加上*一个由正弦、余弦交替组成的**位置向量**，模型拿到的向量就同时含有这个词*是什么*和*在哪*。位置 0 的 the 和位置 3 的 the 现在向量不同了。

text.en: The table is the first sine/cosine pair (the one drawn in the lecture); other pairs use slower frequencies, like the hands of a clock, so every position gets its own pattern. The formula is the original Transformer paper's (Vaswani et al., 2017; textbook, the exam only needs the idea).
text.zh: 表里是第一对正弦/余弦（讲义里画的那一对）；其他对用更慢的频率，像钟表的各根指针，于是每个位置都有独一无二的图案。公式来自原始 Transformer 论文（Vaswani 等，2017；教科书内容，考试只需要想法）。

title.en: Deeper: attention, with queries, keys and weights
title.zh: 深入：注意力里的查询、键和权重

lines.tex: q_i = W_Q x_i, \quad k_j = W_K x_j, \quad v_j = W_V x_j

say.en: Every token makes three vectors with learned matrices. **Query** $q$: what I am looking for ('who am I referring to?'). **Key** $k$: what I can offer. **Value** $v$: the content I hand over if chosen.
say.zh: 每个词元用学出来的矩阵造三个向量。**查询** $q$：我在找什么（“我指的是谁？”）。**键** $k$：我能提供什么。**值** $v$：被选中时交出去的内容。

say.en: Compare the query of token $i$ with the key of token $j$ by a dot product: a better match gives a bigger score. Dividing by $\sqrt{d}$ stops scores growing with the vector size $d$.
say.zh: 用点积比较词 $i$ 的查询和词 $j$ 的键：匹配越好，分数越大。除以 $\sqrt{d}$ 是为了不让分数随向量维度 $d$ 变大。

say.en: Softmax over the tokens: positive weights that sum to 1. These are the line thicknesses in the lecture's picture (.45 on 'trophy', .15 on 'big'). It is the same softmax as in InfoNCE, with $\sqrt{d}$ playing the role of the temperature.
say.zh: 对各词做 softmax：权重为正且和为 1。就是讲义图里线的粗细（trophy 上 .45，big 上 .15）。和 InfoNCE 里是同一个 softmax，只是 $\sqrt{d}$ 扮演了温度。

say.en: The new vector of token $i$ is the weighted mix of the values. 'it' now carries information from 'trophy': a **contextually rich embedding**.
say.zh: 词 $i$ 的新向量是各值按权重的加权和。现在“it”带上了“trophy”的信息：**富含上下文的嵌入**。

say.en: Toy numbers (not the lecture's), $d = 2$: $q = (1, 0.5)$ for 'it'; keys trophy $(2,1)$, suitcase $(1,1)$, big $(0,1)$. Dot products 2.5, 1.5, 0.5, each divided by $\sqrt{2}$.
Softmax of the three scores. 'trophy' wins.
say.zh: 对三个分数做 softmax。trophy 胜出。

say.en: With one-number values 4, 1, 2 the output is dominated by the trophy's value.
say.zh: 取一维的值 4、1、2，输出主要由 trophy 的值决定。

intro.en: When the model reads 'it', each other word is asked how relevant it is. Query against keys, then mix.
intro.zh: 模型读到“it”时，要问其他每个词有多相关。用查询去对键，然后混合。

outro.en: In practice several attention sets run in parallel (multi-head), and in a decoder the weights on *later* tokens are forced to zero, so the model cannot peek at the word it must predict.
outro.zh: 实际中会并行跑多组注意力（多头）；解码器里对*后面*词元的权重被强制为零，模型就不能偷看要预测的那个词。

prompt.en: Write the weight on 'trophy' from the three dot products 2.5, 1.5, 0.5.
prompt.zh: 由三个点积 2.5、1.5、0.5 写出 trophy 的权重。

title.en: The Transformer block and how text is generated
title.zh: Transformer 模块与文本生成

rows.en: each token (vocabulary item) becomes a dense vector
rows.zh: 每个词元（词表项）变成稠密向量
N 层 [注意力, 前馈]

rows.en: each with layer norm and a residual connection (the stream that carries the vector); attention adds context
rows.zh: 各带层归一化和残差连接（携带向量的主干）；注意力加入上下文

rows.en: projects the hidden vector to one score per vocabulary word
rows.zh: 把隐藏向量投影成词表里每个词一个分数

items.en: Feed the whole context $x_1..x_T$ to the decoder.
items.zh: 把整个上下文 $x_1..x_T$ 喂给解码器。

items.en: Get $p(w \mid x_1..x_T)$ over the vocabulary.
items.zh: 得到词表上的 $p(w \mid x_1..x_T)$。

items.en: Choose $x_{T+1}$ from it (greedy, top-k or top-p).
items.zh: 从中选出 $x_{T+1}$（贪心、top-k 或 top-p）。

items.en: Append it to the context, $T \leftarrow T+1$, repeat until the end-of-sequence token.
items.zh: 把它接到上下文后面，$T \leftarrow T+1$，重复直到出现结束符。

text.en: Next-word distribution after 'the cat sat on the': mat 0.45, floor 0.25, sofa 0.15, roof 0.10, moon 0.05.
text.zh: “the cat sat on the”之后的下一词分布：mat 0.45、floor 0.25、sofa 0.15、roof 0.10、moon 0.05。

rows.zh: 概率最高的 k 个，重新归一化

rows.en: the smallest set whose cumulative probability exceeds p, renormalised
rows.zh: 累计概率超过 p 的最小集合，重新归一化

text.en: Greedy is repeatable but dull; sampling gives variety, and top-k / top-p stop it picking absurd rare tokens.
text.zh: 贪心可重复但呆板；采样带来多样性，top-k / top-p 则避免抽到离谱的罕见词。

title.en: From a pre-trained model to an assistant
title.zh: 从预训练模型到助手

items.en: **Pre-train** on raw, unlabelled text by next-token prediction. GPT-1 (Radford) and BERT (Devlin) both appeared around 2018: GPT predicts left to right; BERT, 'bidirectional', fills in masked words using both sides.
items.zh: 在原始无标注文本上用下一词预测**预训练**。GPT-1（Radford）和 BERT（Devlin）都出现在 2018 年前后：GPT 从左到右预测；BERT 是“双向”的，用两侧上下文补出被遮的词。

items.en: **It learns tasks without being told.** To predict the next word well across billions of sentences the model must learn facts, reasoning, language and common sense. Raw web text already contains tasks matched together, such as a question followed by its answer. GPT-3 needed no extra supervised learning: just predict the next token.
items.zh: **没人教它也学到了任务。** 要在数十亿句子上把下一个词预测好，模型必须学会事实、推理、语言和常识。原始网页文本里本来就有成对的任务，比如问题后面跟着答案。GPT-3 不需要额外的监督学习：只预测下一个词元。

items.en: **Fine-tune** so that it answers questions (not just completes sentences), follows instructions and behaves safely. Alignment methods named in the lecture: prompt-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), adapters / parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
items.zh: **微调**，让它会回答问题（而不只是续写句子）、遵循指令、行为安全。讲义提到的对齐方法：提示调优 (prompt-tuning)、基于人类反馈的强化学习 (RLHF)、适配器/参数高效微调。

title.en: What an LLM is (the lecture summary)
title.zh: 大语言模型是什么（讲义小结）

body.en: A Transformer with many layers (50 or more blocks), used as an autoregressive decoder, pre-trained in a self-supervised way, then trained and aligned further. It is not a new paradigm: it is self-supervised learning at enormous scale.
body.zh: 一个层数很多（50 块以上）的 Transformer，当作自回归解码器使用，用自监督方式预训练，再进一步训练和对齐。它不是新范式：是规模巨大的自监督学习。

text.en: Scale (lecture): roughly 10 TB of text, 6,000 GPUs for 12 days, about \$2M and 10²⁴ FLOPs, giving a parameter file of about 140 GB. It is so expensive that the weights are updated only once a year or every few years.
text.zh: 规模（讲义）：约 10 TB 文本、6000 块 GPU 跑 12 天、约 200 万美元、10²⁴ 次浮点运算，得到约 140 GB 的参数文件。贵到权重一年甚至几年才更新一次。

title.en: Pros and cons of self-supervised learning
title.zh: 自监督学习的优缺点

rows.en: No labelling cost for pre-training: raw data is abundant
rows.zh: 预训练不需要标注成本：原始数据很充裕

rows.en: Needs a well-designed pretext task / augmentation; a poor one learns the wrong thing or a shortcut
rows.zh: 要精心设计前置任务/增强；设计不好会学错东西或走捷径

rows.en: Big unlabelled data gives general representations that transfer to many tasks
rows.zh: 大量无标注数据学出通用表示，可迁移到很多任务

rows.en: Very expensive in data and compute (the LLM numbers above)
rows.zh: 数据和算力都很贵（见上面大模型的数字）

rows.en: The downstream task needs only a few labels and a small head
rows.zh: 下游任务只需少量标签和一个小头

rows.en: Quality is judged indirectly, only through the downstream task
rows.zh: 质量只能通过下游任务间接评判

rows.en: Scales: more data and bigger models keep improving it
rows.zh: 可扩展：数据更多、模型更大就持续变好

rows.en: Learns the biases of its data; contrastive methods need many negatives and suffer from false negatives
rows.zh: 会学到数据里的偏差；对比方法需要很多负样本，且受假负样本困扰

title.en: Which one is self-supervised?
title.zh: 哪一个是自监督？

prompt.en: Which of these is self-supervised learning?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一个是自监督学习？

label.en: Self-training: label the unlabelled data with the model, then retrain
label.zh: 自训练：用模型给无标注数据打标签，再重训

feedback.en: That is semi-supervised: it starts from a labelled set and the pseudo-labels come from the *model's predictions*, not from the structure of the data.
feedback.zh: 那是半监督：它从一个有标注的集合出发，伪标签来自*模型的预测*，而不是数据本身的结构。

label.en: Hide 15% of the words in a text and train the model to recover them
label.zh: 遮住文本里 15% 的词，训练模型把它们还原

label.en: Run k-means on unlabelled images to find groups
label.zh: 对无标注图像做 k-means 找簇

feedback.en: k-means has no target built from the data; it is unsupervised.
feedback.zh: k-means 没有从数据造出的目标；它是无监督。

label.en: Ask an expert to label the images the model is least sure of
label.zh: 请专家给模型最没把握的图像打标签

feedback.en: That is active learning: the labels still come from a human.
feedback.zh: 那是主动学习：标签仍然来自人。

explain.en: The text itself supplies the answers (the masked words), so no human labelled anything, and there is a target and a loss.
explain.zh: 文本自己提供了答案（被遮的词），没有人标注，且有目标和损失。

title.en: InfoNCE by hand
title.zh: 手算 InfoNCE

prompt.en: An anchor has cosine similarities (0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.0) with its positive and three negatives, in that order. With temperature τ = 0.5, compute the InfoNCE loss (natural log). Round to 3 decimals.
prompt.zh: 一个锚点和它的正样本及三个负样本的余弦相似度依次为 (0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.0)。温度 τ = 0.5，求 InfoNCE 损失（自然对数）。保留 3 位小数。

title.en: Lowering the temperature
title.zh: 降低温度

prompt.en: In the InfoNCE loss, what is the main effect of making the temperature τ much smaller?
prompt.zh: 在 InfoNCE 损失中，把温度 τ 调得很小，主要效果是什么？

label.en: All negatives are weighted equally
label.zh: 所有负样本权重相等

feedback.en: That is the large-τ limit, where softmax is flat.
feedback.zh: 那是 τ 很大时的极限，softmax 趋平。

label.en: The positive pair is pulled together less
label.zh: 正样本对被拉近的力度变小

feedback.en: The pull on the positive is $(1-p_0)/\tau$; it does not weaken because τ is small.
feedback.zh: 对正样本的拉力是 $(1-p_0)/\tau$，不会因 τ 小而变弱。

label.en: The gradient concentrates on the hardest negatives, which also makes false negatives hurt more
label.zh: 梯度集中在最难的负样本上，因此假负样本的伤害也更大

label.en: The loss becomes independent of the negatives
label.zh: 损失变得与负样本无关

feedback.en: The negatives stay in the denominator; only the *hardest* ones dominate it.
feedback.zh: 负样本仍在分母里，只是*最难*的那些占了主导。

explain.en: A small τ makes softmax nearly an argmax: the push goes to the most similar negative, which may really be a same-class instance.
explain.zh: τ 小则 softmax 接近 argmax：推力给了最相似的负样本，而它很可能其实是同类样本。

title.en: Why next-token prediction is self-supervised
title.zh: 为什么下一词预测属于自监督

prompt.en: Why is training a GPT-style model on raw text called self-supervised?
prompt.zh: 为什么在原始文本上训练 GPT 类模型称为自监督？

label.en: Annotators write the next word for each context
label.zh: 标注员为每个上下文写出下一个词

feedback.en: No annotator is involved; the text already contains the next word.
feedback.zh: 没有标注员；文本里本来就有下一个词。

label.en: The model labels its own outputs and learns from them
label.zh: 模型给自己的输出打标签再学习

feedback.en: That is self-training (semi-supervised). Here the target is the real next token in the data, not the model's guess.
feedback.zh: 那是自训练（半监督）。这里的目标是数据里真实的下一个词元，不是模型的猜测。

label.en: It is unsupervised: there is no loss function
label.zh: 它是无监督：没有损失函数

feedback.en: There is a loss: cross-entropy with the true next token.
feedback.zh: 有损失：与真实下一词元的交叉熵。

label.en: The target (the next token) is taken from the data itself, so no human labels are needed
label.zh: 目标（下一个词元）取自数据本身，不需要人工标注

explain.en: Every position of every text is a free (context, next word) example.
explain.zh: 每段文本的每个位置都是一个免费的（上下文，下一个词）样本。

title.en: Top-p sampling
title.zh: top-p 采样

prompt.en: After 'the cat sat on the' the model gives: mat 0.45, floor 0.25, sofa 0.15, roof 0.10, moon 0.05. With top-p sampling, p = 0.8, what is the probability of 'mat' after renormalising? Round to 3 decimals.
prompt.zh: “the cat sat on the”之后模型给出：mat 0.45、floor 0.25、sofa 0.15、roof 0.10、moon 0.05。用 p = 0.8 的 top-p 采样，重新归一化后 mat 的概率是多少？保留 3 位小数。

explain.en: Cumulative: 0.45, 0.70, 0.85. The smallest set exceeding 0.8 is {mat, floor, sofa} (total 0.85). Renormalise: 0.45 / 0.85 = 0.529.

title.en: SSL vs unsupervised vs semi-supervised
title.zh: SSL 对比无监督、半监督

prompt.en: In 2-3 lines: how does self-supervised learning differ from unsupervised and from semi-supervised learning?
prompt.zh: 用 2-3 行回答：自监督学习与无监督、半监督有什么区别？

key_points.en: Self-supervised builds a target (label) from the data itself and trains with a loss, like supervised learning
key_points.zh: 自监督：目标（标签）由数据自己造，用损失训练，像监督学习

key_points.en: Unsupervised has no target: it finds structure (clusters, density)
key_points.zh: 无监督：没有目标，找结构（簇、密度）

key_points.en: Semi-supervised uses a few human labels together with many unlabelled instances in one training
key_points.zh: 半监督：在同一次训练里把少量人工标签和大量无标注样本一起用

key_points.en: Self-supervised pre-trains a representation on unlabelled data, then a few labels are used for the downstream task
key_points.zh: 自监督：先在无标注数据上预训练表示，再用少量标签做下游任务

model_answer.en: Self-supervised learning creates its own labels from the data (e.g. a masked word or the next token) and trains with a normal loss, aiming at a representation that is reused later with a few labels. Unsupervised learning has no target at all and just finds structure such as clusters. Semi-supervised learning mixes a few human labels with many unlabelled instances in a single training procedure.
model_answer.zh: Self-supervised learning creates its own labels from the data (e.g. a masked word or the next token) and trains with a normal loss, aiming at a representation that is reused later with a few labels. Unsupervised learning has no target at all and just finds structure such as clusters. Semi-supervised learning mixes a few human labels with many unlabelled instances in a single training procedure.

explain.en: Marking: the target comes from the data (SSL) vs no target (unsupervised) vs few human labels used together with unlabelled data (semi).
explain.zh: 评分点：目标来自数据（SSL）、没有目标（无监督）、少量人工标签与无标注数据一起用（半监督）。

title.en: Design: X-rays with few labels (Section C style)
title.zh: 设计题：标注很少的 X 光片（C 部分风格）

prompt.en: A hospital has 2 million unlabelled chest X-rays and only 300 with a diagnosis label. Design a self-supervised approach to build a diagnosis classifier. Say which pretext task and augmentations you would use, what you freeze, how you evaluate, and one risk.
prompt.zh: 一家医院有 200 万张无标注胸片，只有 300 张有诊断标签。设计一个自监督方案来建诊断分类器。说明用什么前置任务和增强、冻结什么、怎么评估，以及一个风险。

key_points.en: Pretext on the 2M unlabelled images: masked patch reconstruction or contrastive learning with augmentations
key_points.zh: 在 200 万无标注图上做前置任务：遮块还原，或带增强的对比学习

key_points.en: Augmentations chosen so that diagnostic information survives (small crops, mild brightness/contrast; not strong colour or flips that change anatomy)
key_points.zh: 增强要保住诊断信息（小裁剪、轻微亮度/对比度；不用改变解剖结构的强烈变色或翻转）

key_points.en: Pre-train the encoder, freeze it, train a small classifier head on the 300 labels (linear probe), optionally fine-tune with a small learning rate
key_points.zh: 预训练编码器，冻结，用 300 个标签训练小分类头（线性探测），可选再用小学习率微调

key_points.en: Evaluate on a held-out labelled set from other patients / hospitals, compare with training from scratch on the 300 labels
key_points.zh: 在其他病人/医院的留出标注集上评估，并与只用 300 个标签从头训练作比较

key_points.en: Risk: shortcut (scanner or text markers learned), augmentation removing the sign, or bias of the data
key_points.zh: 风险：走捷径（学到机器或文字标记）、增强抹掉病征、数据偏差

model_answer.en: Pre-train an encoder on the 2M unlabelled X-rays, either by reconstructing masked patches or contrastively (two augmented views of one X-ray are a positive pair, other patients are negatives). I would use mild augmentations (small crops, brightness and contrast jitter) so that the diagnostic signs survive, and avoid ones that change anatomy. Then freeze the encoder and train a small classifier head on the 300 labels (a linear probe), perhaps fine-tuning later with a small learning rate. I would evaluate on a held-out labelled set from different patients or hospitals and compare with a model trained from scratch on the 300 labels. Main risk: the encoder learns shortcuts such as scanner artefacts or text markers, or the pre-training data is biased towards one hospital.
model_answer.zh: Pre-train an encoder on the 2M unlabelled X-rays, either by reconstructing masked patches or contrastively (two augmented views of one X-ray are a positive pair, other patients are negatives). I would use mild augmentations (small crops, brightness and contrast jitter) so that the diagnostic signs survive, and avoid ones that change anatomy. Then freeze the encoder and train a small classifier head on the 300 labels (a linear probe), perhaps fine-tuning later with a small learning rate. I would evaluate on a held-out labelled set from different patients or hospitals and compare with a model trained from scratch on the 300 labels. Main risk: the encoder learns shortcuts such as scanner artefacts or text markers, or the pre-training data is biased towards one hospital.

explain.en: A strong answer links each choice to the pipeline: pretext, augmentation as bias, frozen encoder plus head, fair evaluation, risk.
explain.zh: 好答案把每个选择对应到流程：前置任务、作为偏置的增强、冻结编码器加小头、公平评估、风险。

title.en: What to remember
title.zh: 要记住的

items.en: **SSL:** make labels from the data (hide, corrupt, relate, next word); stage 1 pretext on unlabelled data → encoder; stage 2 frozen encoder + small head on few labels (or fine-tune).
items.zh: **SSL：** 用数据自己造标签（遮挡、破坏、关系、下一个词）；第一阶段在无标注数据上做前置任务 → 编码器；第二阶段冻结编码器加小头，用少量标签（或微调）。

items.en: **Three families:** masked prediction, contrastive (same/different), autoregressive (next token).
items.zh: **三类：** 遮挡预测、对比（相同/不同）、自回归（下一词）。

items.en: **vs others:** unsupervised has no target; semi-supervised mixes few labels with unlabelled data in one training; active asks a human for labels.
items.zh: **对比：** 无监督没有目标；半监督在一次训练里混用少量标签和无标注数据；主动学习向人要标签。

items.en: Numerator pulls the positive, denominator pushes everything; low τ focuses on hard (and false) negatives; $\mathcal{L} = \ln(K+1)$ at no discrimination.
items.zh: 分子拉正样本，分母推所有；τ 低则聚焦难（和假）负样本；毫无区分时 $\mathcal{L} = \ln(K+1)$。

items.en: **Next-token loss** $= -\sum_t \ln p(x_t \mid x_{<t})$: self-supervised, MLE of the text.
items.zh: **下一词损失** $= -\sum_t \ln p(x_t \mid x_{<t})$：自监督，文本的极大似然。

items.en: **Transformer:** positional encoding (order) + attention softmax(q·k/√d) mixing values (relations) + unembedding + softmax; decode by greedy / top-k / top-p until eos.
items.zh: **Transformer：** 位置编码（顺序）+ 注意力 softmax(q·k/√d) 混合值（关系）+ 反嵌入 + softmax；用贪心/top-k/top-p 解码直到 eos。

items.en: **LLM:** pre-train (self-supervised) then fine-tune / align (prompt-tuning, RLHF, adapters).
items.zh: **大模型：** 预训练（自监督）再微调/对齐（提示调优、RLHF、适配器）。
